memory_candidates: Lean4: a `simp only [defName1, defName2, ...] at h` that unfolds a function definition may still leave the result frozen at an `if`/`Option.getD` layer if those specific reduction lemmas aren't in the given list -- `simp only [..., Option.getD, reduceIte] at h` (or just unrestricted `simp at h`) is often needed in addition to the definition names themselves.

Lean4: `Formula.complexity`-style recursive functions with special-cased nested match patterns (e.g. Lukasiewicz-encoded operators) get stuck reducing `(phi.imp psi).complexity` when phi is a still-abstract IsPropositional-bound variable and psi is literally a concrete constructor like `.bot` -- the match can't rule out phi being shaped like the special pattern's required sub-term. Fix: a dedicated lemma `cases hphi <;> cases hpsi <;> rfl` proven once, applied explicitly (not via bare unqualified simp, which won't auto-discharge the IsPropositional side-conditions) at each stuck site.

Lean4: do NOT `cases` an ambient hypothesis inside a nested `(by ...)` tactic-block argument if that same hypothesis is ALSO referenced elsewhere in the surrounding term -- the destructive cases corrupts the outer term's later reference via shared local-context/metavariable capture, even though the `by` block's own goal is nominally isolated.

Lean4: `cases hpsi' with | imp _ _ => ... hpsi' ...` is a hard error -- cases on a hypothesis destroys it, so anonymous-pattern arms (`_ _`) that don't bind the constructor's components cannot reconstruct the original hypothesis afterward. Name the components (`| imp hc hd =>`) and rebuild via the constructor (`IsPropositional.imp hc hd`) if the original proof term is still needed.

Lean4: `List.forall_mem_cons` applied to a 2-element list `[a, b]` produces a 3-part nested conjunction `a-in-b and (b-in-b and (forall x in [], x-in-b))`, not a flat 2-part pair -- `obtain <x, y> := h` silently mis-binds `y` to the whole trailing pair. Use `obtain <x, y, -> := h` to discard the trivial tail.
